overview: This record begins in 1945, when the Republic of China still governed and civil war was about to resume. The People’s Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949. These are distinct political phases. The imported outline spans changing governments and territorial control; it cannot resolve sovereignty disputes or substitute for the separate Taiwan record.

periods.title: War ends, civil war returns
periods.summary: Nationalists and Communists failed to establish a lasting post-war settlement.

periods.title: A new government and social campaigns
periods.summary: The People’s Republic was founded in 1949; the 1950 marriage law sought to change family relations.

periods.title: Great Leap and famine
periods.summary: Communes and production campaigns were followed by the devastating famine of 1959 to 1961.

periods.title: Cultural Revolution and transition
periods.summary: The Cultural Revolution of 1966 to 1976 disrupted education; a different reform era followed.

periods.title: Reform and opening
periods.summary: Economic reforms expanded household farming decisions, rural enterprises and foreign investment.

periods.title: Repression and continued transformation
periods.summary: The military crackdown in 1989 demonstrated the violent limits placed on political dissent.

periods.title: Global connections and new challenges
periods.summary: WTO membership began in December 2001; later social and scientific examples are individually dated.

items.text: Japan’s defeat in 1945 did not bring lasting peace to China. Nationalists and Communists returned to full-scale civil war. Mao Zedong proclaimed the People’s Republic in October 1949, while the Nationalist government retreated to Taiwan. This was a change of government on the mainland, not the disappearance of Chinese people or culture.

The Communist Party became the leading institution of the People’s Republic. A 2025 Congressional Research Service account explains that Party authorities outrank government counterparts, while the State Council handles administration and the National People’s Congress passes laws and budgets. The Party’s influence extends through national and local institutions.

The Great Leap Forward tried to transform production rapidly. Communal farming and dining changed everyday routines, but the famine of 1959 to 1961 brought catastrophic hunger and deaths. Research identifies state grain procurement and failures to respond to real conditions as major causes; abundant grain in an area did not guarantee food for its residents.

During the Cultural Revolution, schools and universities suffered major interruptions. Researchers have traced differences in later educational attainment to the disruption experienced by different cities and age groups between 1966 and 1976. A child’s chance to keep studying could depend on political upheaval well beyond the classroom.

A 1967 poster preserved by the Library of Congress shows Red Guard youths destroying symbols of older traditions, including books and religion. It reveals how propaganda encouraged cultural destruction. An image intended to recruit enthusiasm has become evidence for historians examining a damaging political campaign.

Reforms associated with the turn beginning in 1978 experimented with markets, rural enterprises and overseas investment. The first four special economic zones were created in 1980. Change developed through experiments and adjustments rather than a single moment when the whole economy switched systems.

In June 1989, troops violently suppressed protests in Beijing, killing civilians. Declassified documents collected by the National Security Archive show military attacks and officials’ fear that dissent threatened Party rule. Economic change did not automatically produce freedom to challenge the government.

The 1950 Marriage Law promoted choosing one’s own spouse, monogamy and equal legal rights for women and men. Couples were required to register marriages with state offices. Posters advertised happy families, but the law also met resistance and generated disputes: a new rule did not instantly rearrange every household.

Family size also became a matter of government policy. Birth restrictions changed over time; UNFPA recorded a universal two-child policy in 2016 and a three-child policy announced in 2021. Its 2021 discussion stressed reproductive rights and support for families, rather than treating parents simply as tools for population targets.

Under the household responsibility system, farm families gained more control over production and could keep output after meeting agreed delivery and tax obligations. They received land-use rights, not unrestricted private ownership of farmland. The rules changed the relationship between daily effort, household decisions and income.

Jobs could also separate families. In a February 2026 UNICEF account, Zhang Qin in rural Guizhou was caring for grandchildren while their parents worked in Jiangsu. Video calls helped keep them connected. Grandparents’ daily work included play, comfort and learning, as well as food and clothes.

Spring Festival preparations include cleaning homes, laying in provisions and making food for reunion dinners. Families may stay awake to welcome the new year and visit relatives and neighbours. Skills pass between generations through cooking, decorations and performance: celebrations can be a lively family classroom.

Tea is both a craft and a way to welcome people. Producers make varieties such as green, white, oolong and black tea, while families and apprentices pass on processing skills. UNESCO also records the pastries served alongside tea. One plant can lead to a surprisingly complicated drinks menu.

At Doujiang Primary School in Guangxi, a 2009 UNICEF report described a “My Voice” noticeboard where pupils posted requests and criticism. They asked for dance lessons and more trees, and even complained about boring lectures. The children also managed sports equipment: responsibility could start with making sure the next class got its ball back.

Cold-weather sanitation needed its own engineering. At Taizi Township Central School in Qinghai, new facilities reported in 2023 used solar energy to warm handwashing water. Private stalls, more provision for girls and an accessible room addressed dignity and access as well as cleanliness. A warm tap can be an important school improvement.

Rural health care expanded through community workers often called barefoot doctors. They combined farming with short medical training, prevention and basic treatment. The name became popular in the 1960s; WHO’s 2008 history also describes later examinations through which workers could qualify as village doctors. Training and responsibilities changed over time.

Tu Youyou’s team searched for a new treatment for malaria. Her first-person Nobel account describes an effective wormwood extract in 1971 and the isolation of artemisinin in 1972. This required laboratory tests, clinical research and cooperation between institutes; an old medical clue became part of a modern drug-development programme.

Even a promising medicine could fail because of how its tablets were made. Tu recalled that early artemisinin tablets were too hard to break apart properly. The team investigated and tested capsules in 1973. The useful discovery was not just the molecule: how to deliver it mattered too.

China joined the World Trade Organization on 11 December 2001 after a long negotiation process. Membership connected its economy more formally to a system of international trade agreements. This milestone belongs to modern economic history, rather than to the much earlier Silk Roads.

A World Bank study published in 2019 documented more than 25,000 kilometres of high-speed railway by the end of 2017. These lines linked major cities and helped change passenger travel. The number is a dated snapshot of a rapidly expanding network, not its present-day length.

The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first samples from the Moon’s far side on 25 June 2024. Its lander also carried a small laser reflector developed by Chinese and Italian researchers. Collecting rocks and providing a reflector for future precision measurements were different scientific jobs aboard the same mission.

The returned lunar material gave researchers direct evidence of ancient volcanic activity on the far side. A November 2024 report described rock evidence for episodes roughly 2.8 and 4.2 billion years ago. Small samples can answer questions about a world far larger than the container that holds them.

Economic growth brought enormous reductions in severe poverty. A 2022 World Bank report estimated that almost 800 million fewer people lived below its then-used international threshold of $1.90 a day than forty years earlier. That specific measure does not mean hardship or inequality had disappeared.

A 1950 marriage-law poster is catalogued as “拥护婚姻法” (Yonghu hunyinfa), translated “Support the marriage law.” These are the catalogue’s modern-character transcription and romanization. The poster shows a couple shaking hands, with the law’s twenty-seven articles printed on the back: public information came on both sides of the paper.

Tu Youyou’s 2015 Nobel biography writes “青蒿素” (qīnghāosù), the Chinese name for artemisinin. This short scientific term is an attested modern Chinese writing sample tied to the malaria research described above. It names the purified drug compound, not simply a cup of herbal tea.

ending.text: The People’s Republic continues; this record has no historical fall date. Political institutions and everyday conditions keep changing, so modern examples here are dated. The map’s changing outlines should not be used to settle the status of Taiwan or other contested territories.
